curriculum_title: TechVerse Hub — Full Stack Web Development Curriculum

modules.title: Introduction To Web Development
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module, the student understands what happens from the moment a user types a URL to the moment pixels appear on screen — and knows where their future code fits in that chain.

modules.title: HTML Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module, the student can build a fully structured, semantic, accessible, and SEO-conscious web page from scratch using only HTML — no styling, no JavaScript — and understand exactly why each element choice matters.

modules.title: CSS Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module, the student can take any HTML page and make it fully styled, responsive across all screen sizes, and visually polished — understanding exactly why every style decision works the way it does, not just copying properties until something looks right.

modules.title: JavaScript Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end, the student can write real JS programs - manipulating the DOM, handling events, fetching API data, managing async code with async/await, and building complete Vanilla JS applications without a framework.

modules.title: Git, Workflow And Vanilla JS Projects
lesson_titles: Local Storage And State Management Basics
Advanced Git — Undoing Things And History
Conventional Commits, CI Basics, And Module Wrap-Up
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student operates like a professional developer: writing code in a configured editor, tracking every change in Git, collaborating via GitHub with proper branch-based workflow, and shipping polished multi-file Vanilla JS projects with clean, linted code.

modules.title: React Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can build complete React applications from scratch — creating reusable components, managing state with hooks, handling events, fetching and rendering API data, and thinking in the React mental model of unidirectional data flow.

modules.title: Backend Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can build a complete REST API with Node.js and Express — handling all HTTP methods, using middleware correctly, connecting to a database, validating input, handling errors properly, and following the engineering principles that make server-side code secure and maintainable.

modules.title: Database Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can design appropriate data schemas for real-world applications, perform all CRUD operations in both MongoDB (with Mongoose) and PostgreSQL (with raw SQL), understand when to choose each database type, and avoid the most common data modeling mistakes.

modules.title: Authentication Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can build a complete, secure authentication system — user registration with hashed passwords, JWT-based login, protected API routes with middleware, role-based access control, secure cookie handling, and the security thinking behind every decision.

modules.title: Full Stack Application Basics
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can build and deploy a complete full stack CRUD application — React frontend fetching from an Express/MongoDB backend with JWT authentication, environment-specific configuration, and professional error handling across both layers.

modules.title: TypeScript Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student writes all JavaScript with TypeScript — typed React components, typed Express handlers, typed Mongoose models, and typed API responses — and understands how types serve as living documentation that keeps large codebases maintainable.

modules.title: Next.js Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student understands Next.js App Router architecture, can build full stack applications with Server Components, Client Components, and API Routes, chooses the correct rendering strategy for each page, and deploys to Vercel with confidence.

modules.title: Advanced React Architecture
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can architect React applications with reusable custom hooks, compound components, context-based state, performance-optimized renders, lazy-loaded routes, and production-ready error boundaries — and knows exactly when each pattern is and isn't the right tool.

modules.title: Routing Systems
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can implement complete React Router v6 routing — nested layouts, protected routes, dynamic params, programmatic navigation, search params, and data loading with loaders — and understands when client-side routing applies vs Next.js App Router file-based routing.

modules.title: Advanced State Management
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can architect state management for a production React application — using TanStack Query for all server data, Zustand for global client state, and URL state for shareable UI — and can explain the reasoning behind every decision.

modules.title: API Integration
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student builds a production-grade API client with Axios, handles all HTTP scenarios (loading, error, retry, refresh), integrates real-time updates, designs the API layer for testability, and understands WebSocket-based communication for live features.

modules.title: Backend Architecture
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student architects an Express backend with clear separation between the HTTP layer, business logic layer, and data layer — writes testable services, applies SOLID principles to route and service design, and implements cross-cutting concerns (logging, validation, rate limiting) through composable middleware.

modules.title: Database Engineering
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can design efficient database schemas, write complex aggregation pipelines, use PostgreSQL advanced features (transactions, JSONB, full-text search), manage schema evolution with migrations, identify and fix slow queries, and implement Redis caching to reduce database load.

modules.title: Authentication Systems
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can architect and implement a complete production-grade authentication system — OAuth 2.0 flows, MFA, granular RBAC, secure token handling, account security features, and the threat model that drives every design decision.

modules.title: Testing
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can write comprehensive tests for a full stack application — unit-testing services with mocked dependencies, integration-testing API routes with a test database, component-testing React with Testing Library, and end-to-end testing user flows with Playwright — and can evaluate test coverage to identify gaps.

modules.title: System Design Fundamentals
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can approach any system design problem — decompose requirements, identify bottlenecks before they happen, choose appropriate data stores, design for scale and failure, estimate capacity, and communicate architectural decisions clearly — the core skills of a senior engineer.

modules.title: Advanced Backend Engineering
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can design and implement event-driven systems with message queues, build GraphQL and gRPC services, architect WebSocket infrastructure for real-time features at scale, and apply the production engineering practices that keep backend services reliable under load.

modules.title: Distributed Systems
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student understands the fundamental challenges of distributed computing, can reason about consistency and availability tradeoffs, implement distributed coordination patterns, design for partial failure, and explain how production distributed systems (databases, caches, message queues) solve these problems internally.

modules.title: Security Engineering
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can identify and remediate the OWASP Top 10 vulnerability classes in real code, perform basic threat modeling on a system design, implement secrets management and least-privilege infrastructure, and reason about security tradeoffs the way a security-conscious senior engineer does.

modules.title: AI Engineering
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can integrate LLM APIs into a full stack application with proper error handling and cost control, design effective prompts and structured outputs, build a RAG pipeline for grounding model responses in custom data, implement basic tool-using agents, and reason about the safety and reliability tradeoffs unique to AI features.

modules.title: DevOps And Kubernetes
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can containerize a full stack application with Docker, build automated CI/CD pipelines, understand and use core Kubernetes concepts to deploy and scale containerized applications, and apply infrastructure-as-code principles to manage cloud resources reproducibly.

modules.title: Advanced Frontend
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can choose and implement the right rendering strategy for a given product, profile and optimize frontend performance using real metrics, architect large frontend codebases for scale, implement advanced accessibility patterns, and apply production-grade frontend engineering practices used at senior level.

modules.title: Realtime At Scale
lesson_titles: The Scaling Challenge Of Realtime Connections
Scaling Message Queues For Realtime Workloads
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can architect a realtime system that scales horizontally across multiple server instances, implement reliable message delivery with appropriate guarantees, build presence and collaborative features, and reason about the tradeoffs unique to stateful, long-lived connections at scale.

modules.title: Database Scaling
lesson_titles: Database Capacity Planning And Cost Optimization
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can design a sharding strategy appropriate to a given data access pattern, architect multi-region database deployments with appropriate consistency tradeoffs, plan and execute zero-downtime schema migrations at scale, and make informed build-vs-buy decisions for database scaling using managed distributed database services.

modules.title: Observability
lesson_titles: Service Level Objectives And Error Budgets
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can design a structured logging strategy for a production system, define and track meaningful SLOs and error budgets, debug complex production incidents systematically using observability data, and build the dashboards and alerting that support genuinely actionable on-call operations.

modules.title: Software Architecture
lesson_titles: API Design At The Architectural Level
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student can evaluate architectural styles (monolith, microservices, modular monolith) against real requirements, document architectural decisions rigorously, design systems that balance current needs against future flexibility, and communicate architectural tradeoffs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

modules.title: Resume And Career
lesson_titles: Building A Portfolio And GitHub Presence
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student has a polished resume and portfolio showcasing the curriculum's capstone projects, has practiced and prepared for behavioral and technical interviews including system design discussions, understands how to evaluate and negotiate job offers, and has a concrete plan for continued learning and career growth in their first role.

modules.title: Production Projects
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student has taken the Blog Platform from a working application into a production-hardened system with proper security, AI-powered features, scalable infrastructure, observability, and documented architecture — and has practiced the integration work of combining many specialized concerns into one coherent, deployed system, which is itself a distinct and critical skill from understanding each concern in isolation.

modules.title: Senior Capstone
lesson_titles: Receiving And Interpreting An Ambiguous Brief
modules.module_goal: By the end of this module the student has independently scoped, architected, built, secured, deployed, and documented an original production-grade full stack application from an ambiguous brief; has practiced presenting and defending technical decisions under questioning as in a real senior engineering review; and has a complete, curriculum-spanning portfolio and a concrete plan for the next phase of their engineering career.
